title: Restricting cross-origin iframe navigation to external protocols with permissions policy

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body: With recent changes in [Blink](https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/security-dev/c/ctTpIqlSGSE/) and [Gecko](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1565574) opening an external application is now behind an origin-scoped permission, and the user agent will show a prompt to confirm that the user intents to proceed (to choose an application, for example). Firefox (design concept) Edge This prompt is effectively a permission prompt but it doesn't follow some rules of other permission prompts, specifically relating to cross-origin iframes. Here, both Blink and Gecko have switched to using [Permission Delegation](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1x5QejvpyQ71LPWhMLsaM1lWCfSsBsSQ8Dap9kJ6uLv0/edit?ts=5b857603#heading=h.ib6rctasbt3y) in combination with [Permissions Policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-permissions-policy/) to avoid user confusion when a different origin is requesting a permission on a page and to give the top level site control over who can request and access privileged features. We should probably do the same thing for the new protocol handler prompts. Things we would need for this: - We need a Permissions Policy identifier/token. Something like `external-application` or `external-protocol`? It's a bit unclear where that would be recorded/standardized in this case. - Navigation to external protocols would need to be restricted by default in cross-origin frames. Ideally we could disallow it by default, but to ensure web compat we could start by always prompting and never offering a "Always allow" checkbox (though I suppose that is an implementation detail up to the browsers).
